use: Two or more people talking something through to settle it.

example.romaji: ichido futari de chanto hanashiaou yo.
example.ja: 一度二人でちゃんと話し合おうよ。
example.english: Let's sit down and talk it over properly.

examplePolite.romaji: ichido futari de chanto hanashiaimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 一度二人でちゃんと話し合いましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's sit down and talk it over properly.

notes: Hanashiai = a discussion. Soudan suru is asking someone's advice.

english: get through; be understood; connect (a call)
use: Your meaning, your language, or a phone call getting through.

example.romaji: ryokou de eigo ga zenzen tsuujinakatta.
example.ja: 旅行で英語が全然通じなかった。
example.english: On the trip, nobody understood my English at all.

examplePolite.romaji: ryokou de eigo ga zenzen tsuujimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 旅行で英語が全然通じませんでした。
examplePolite.english: On the trip, my English didn't get through at all.

notes: Denwa ga tsuujinai = the call won't go through. Hanashi ga tsuujiru = we understand each other.

use: Teian suru = suggest; mostly a work and planning word.

example.romaji: hitotsu teian ga aru n da kedo.
example.ja: 一つ提案があるんだけど。
example.english: I've got a suggestion.

examplePolite.romaji: hitotsu teian ga aru n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: 一つ提案があるんですが。
examplePolite.english: I have a suggestion.

use: Chuui sareta = I got told off; signs and announcements use chuui for 'caution'.

example.romaji: mata sensei ni chuui sareta.
example.ja: また先生に注意された。
example.english: I got told off by the teacher again.

examplePolite.romaji: mata sensei ni chuui saremashita.
examplePolite.ja: また先生に注意されました。
examplePolite.english: I was told off by the teacher again.

notes: For 'be careful' in speech, ki o tsukete is more usual; chuui shite sounds like a warning.

example.romaji: iitai koto aru nara, hakkiri itte.
example.ja: 言いたいことあるなら、はっきり言って。
example.english: If you've got something to say, say it straight.

examplePolite.romaji: iitai koto ga aru nara, hakkiri itte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 言いたいことがあるなら、はっきり言ってください。
examplePolite.english: If you have something to say, please say it plainly.

notes: Hakkiri itte at the start of a sentence = 'frankly, to be honest'.

english: bring up; start saying; be the first to suggest
use: Often something sudden or awkward: kyuu ni ... tte iidasu.

example.romaji: kare, kyuu ni kaisha yameru tte iidashita n da.
example.ja: 彼、急に会社辞めるって言い出したんだ。
example.english: He suddenly announced he's quitting his job.

examplePolite.romaji: kare ga kyuu ni kaisha o yameru to iidashita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼が急に会社を辞めると言い出したんです。
examplePolite.english: He suddenly announced he's quitting his job.

notes: Iidashippe = whoever suggested it (and so has to do it).

use: Learning from a person: X ni osowaru.

example.romaji: kono ryouri, haha ni osowatta n da.
example.ja: この料理、母に教わったんだ。
example.english: My mum taught me this dish.

examplePolite.romaji: kono ryouri wa haha ni osowarimashita.
examplePolite.ja: この料理は母に教わりました。
examplePolite.english: My mother taught me this dish.

notes: Pairs with oshieru (teach). Narau is close but also covers lessons and classes.

use: Agreeing with a plan or proposal; sansei! alone = 'I'm in!'

example.romaji: minna sansei shiteru kara, sore de ikou.
example.ja: みんな賛成してるから、それで行こう。
example.english: Everyone's for it, so let's go with that.

examplePolite.romaji: minna sansei shite iru node, sore de ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: みんな賛成しているので、それで行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: Everyone's in favour, so let's go with that.

notes: Opposite: hantai (against). To agree with what someone just said, people usually say sou da ne.

english: talk to; start a conversation with
use: Being the one who speaks first: X ni hanashikakeru.

example.romaji: densha de shiranai hito ni hanashikakerareta.
example.ja: 電車で知らない人に話しかけられた。
example.english: A stranger started talking to me on the train.

examplePolite.romaji: densha de shiranai hito ni hanashikakeraremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 電車で知らない人に話しかけられました。
examplePolite.english: A stranger started talking to me on the train.

notes: Ima hanashikakenai de = don't talk to me right now.

use: A long telling-off, usually from a parent or boss; also a sermon.

example.romaji: mata oya ni sekkyou sareta.
example.ja: また親に説教された。
example.english: My parents lectured me again.

examplePolite.romaji: mata oya ni sekkyou saremashita.
examplePolite.ja: また親に説教されました。
examplePolite.english: My parents lectured me again.

notes: Mostly heard in the passive: sekkyou sareta. Chuui is the short version.

example.romaji: uso tsukanai de, honto no koto itte.
example.ja: 嘘つかないで、ほんとのこと言って。
example.english: Don't lie — tell me the truth.

examplePolite.romaji: uso o tsukanai de, hontou no koto o itte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 嘘をつかないで、本当のことを言ってください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't lie — tell me the truth.

notes: Uso! alone = 'no way!' — surprise, not an accusation. Usotsuki = liar.

example.romaji: watashi no koto, shinjite yo.
example.ja: 私のこと、信じてよ。
example.english: Come on, trust me.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi no koto o shinjite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 私のことを信じてください。
examplePolite.english: Please trust me.

use: Feeling a sensation, mood or presence: samusa o kanjiru.

example.romaji: saikin, toshi o kanjiru na.
example.ja: 最近、年を感じるな。
example.english: I'm feeling my age lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin, toshi o kanjimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近、年を感じます。
examplePolite.english: I've been feeling my age lately.

notes: The noun kanji = feeling, vibe: sonna kanji = something like that.

example.romaji: ano hito no namae, omoidasenai.
example.ja: あの人の名前、思い出せない。
example.english: I can't remember that person's name.

examplePolite.romaji: ano kata no namae ga omoidasemasen.
examplePolite.ja: あの方の名前が思い出せません。
examplePolite.english: I can't remember that person's name.

notes: Omoidasu is the moment it comes back; oboete iru is still having it in memory.

english: calm down; settle down; feel at home

example.romaji: daijoubu, ochitsuite yukkuri hanashite.
example.ja: 大丈夫、落ち着いてゆっくり話して。
example.english: It's okay — calm down and talk slowly.

examplePolite.romaji: daijoubu desu, ochitsuite yukkuri hanashite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫です、落ち着いてゆっくり話してください。
examplePolite.english: It's all right — please calm down and speak slowly.

notes: Also 'cozy': kono heya, ochitsuku ne. Shigoto ga ochitsuitara = once work quiets down.

use: Usually describes someone else's visible joy; for your own, say ureshii.

example.romaji: kore agetara, okaasan yorokobu yo.
example.ja: これあげたら、お母さん喜ぶよ。
example.english: Mum will be thrilled if you give her this.

examplePolite.romaji: kore o agetara, okaasan ga yorokobimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: これをあげたら、お母さんが喜びますよ。
examplePolite.english: Your mother will be delighted if you give her this.

example.romaji: kare, zettai machigai mitomenai n da yo.
example.ja: 彼、絶対間違い認めないんだよ。
example.english: He never admits he's wrong.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa zettai ni machigai o mitomenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は絶対に間違いを認めないんです。
examplePolite.english: He never admits he's wrong.

notes: Also 'accept, approve': oya ni mitomete moraenai = my parents won't accept it.

example.romaji: kyuu ni koe kakeru kara odoroita yo.
example.ja: 急に声かけるから驚いたよ。
example.english: You surprised me, calling out like that.

examplePolite.romaji: kyuu ni koe o kakerareta node odorokimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 急に声をかけられたので驚きました。
examplePolite.english: I was surprised when you suddenly called out.

notes: In speech, bikkuri suru is more common; odoroku sounds a little more serious.

use: Means you have no information; for 'I'm not sure', wakaranai is softer.

example.romaji: sonna hito, shiranai yo.
example.ja: そんな人、知らないよ。
example.english: I don't know anyone like that.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna hito wa shirimasen.
examplePolite.ja: そんな人は知りません。
examplePolite.english: I don't know anyone like that.

notes: The negative of shiru; 'I know' is shitte iru (shitteru), never shiru. Shiranai hito = a stranger.

use: Takes an object: ryokou o tanoshimu. 'I had fun' is tanoshikatta.

example.romaji: kyou wa minna de omoikkiri tanoshimou!
example.ja: 今日はみんなで思いっきり楽しもう!
example.english: Let's all really enjoy ourselves today!

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa minna de omoikkiri tanoshimimashou!
examplePolite.ja: 今日はみんなで思いっきり楽しみましょう!
examplePolite.english: Let's all really enjoy ourselves today!

notes: Tanoshimi = something to look forward to: tanoshimi ni shiteru.
